svg.text: A few-step causal draft streams every chunk. A large bidirectional target verifies each chunk with one pass and, when it rejects, writes its own chunk into the draft's KV cache.

g.text: (a) Draft, verify, and correct the cache
lags the cache by one verification
few-step causal student · streams at frame rate
fresh noise between nodes ⇒ Gaussian transition
KV cache (window W · the only channel from past to future)
large bidirectional teacher · consistent, too slow to stream
• at the draft's node σₛ, not a full 40–70-step sample
cost: a small multiple of one draft step; paid once per chunk
exact rule · no retraining of 𝒟 or 𝒯
cache correction: the endorsed chunk is written into 𝒟's KV cache
𝒟 continues from a state 𝒯 endorses, not from its own drift
Over time: what is shown vs. what the draft conditions on
A rejected chunk was shown once (drifted, red),
but the target's chunk is what sits in the cache,
so every later chunk inherits the correction.
At the draft's node σₛ both models see the same noisy chunk
x_{σₛ} and return a clean estimate; re-noising to σₛ₊₁ gives
q = 𝒩((1−σₛ₊₁) ẑ_𝒟, σ²ₛ₊₁ I) p = 𝒩((1−σₛ₊₁) ẑ_𝒯, σ²ₛ₊₁ I)
same covariance, only the mean differs by d = ‖μ_p − μ_q‖.
accept with min{1, p(x)/q(x)}; E[accept] = α = 1 − TV(p,q) = 2Φ(−d / 2σₛ₊₁)
On rejection, sample the residual (p−q)₊ with Gaussian draws only, no extra network call.
Holds only where 𝒟 re-noises with fresh noise, i.e. at its intermediate nodes.
(c) The verified unit decides whether anything is accepted
d² sums over every verified dimension, so d ≈ √D·δ for a per-dimension gap δ,
while the noise scale σ does not grow with D. Hence
α ≈ 2Φ(−√D·δ / 2σ): the same gap δ is accepted or rejected by how much is verified at once
The rule stays exact at every D. Verify chunks or patches, never a clip.
This is why the one prior speculative video generator fell back to a heuristic gate.
